title: Ed Sheeran’s Gillette Stadium Shows Cancelled Amid Extreme Weather, Hollywood Reporter Says
body:
The pop‑rock megastar Ed Sheeran’s two‑night residency at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, has been called off for Friday and Saturday after meteorologists warned that a powerful nor’easter will batter the New England coast with heavy rain, snow and high winds. The decision, announced early Thursday evening, follows a safety‑first assessment by stadium officials and local authorities, who said the storm’s projected intensity could jeopardize both the audience and crew. Ticket holders have been instructed to retain their purchases for a future date or request refunds through the official ticketing platform.

The abrupt cancellation comes at a critical juncture in Sheeran’s “+–=÷×” world tour, which has been a major revenue driver for the artist and a highlight of the summer concert circuit. The shows at Gillette Stadium were slated to attract upwards of 70,000 fans each night, making them among the largest single‑venue performances of the tour. While the weather was the decisive factor, the situation has also revived discussion about recent tensions between the stadium’s owner, New England Patriots founder Robert Kraft, and the originally announced opening act, rapper Macklemore. Kraft reportedly objected to Macklemore’s public statements supporting a “Free Palestine” campaign, prompting the artist’s removal from the bill earlier this month. Although the two issues are unrelated, the convergence of a high‑profile political controversy and a weather‑driven cancellation has amplified media scrutiny of the event.

Industry analysts note that weather‑related disruptions are not uncommon for large‑scale outdoor venues, especially in the volatile climate of the Northeast during late autumn. Nor’easters, which can bring gusts exceeding 60 mph and sudden temperature drops, have forced the postponement of major sporting events and concerts in the past. In this instance, the National Weather Service issued a severe weather warning for the region, predicting snowfall accumulations of 6‑12 inches and wind gusts capable of causing structural damage. Gillette Stadium’s infrastructure, while robust, is not designed to withstand such conditions while hosting tens of thousands of spectators. The decision to cancel, therefore, aligns with standard risk‑management protocols that prioritize public safety over financial considerations.

Fans have taken to social media expressing disappointment, but many also voiced appreciation for the prompt communication from the venue and Sheeran’s team. The artist’s management released a statement emphasizing that the health and safety of fans, crew and local communities are paramount, and pledged to reschedule the shows as soon as feasible. Ticketing partners have set up a dedicated portal for refunds and re‑booking, and several local businesses that were preparing for the influx of concertgoers have announced contingency plans to mitigate the economic impact of the lost weekend.

The cancellation underscores the broader challenges that touring musicians face when navigating unpredictable weather patterns, especially as climate change contributes to more frequent and intense storms. Concert promoters are increasingly investing in advanced forecasting tools and flexible scheduling options to reduce the risk of last‑minute disruptions. Moreover, the episode may prompt venues like Gillette Stadium to explore additional protective measures—such as temporary roofing or reinforced wind barriers—for future high‑capacity events during the fall and winter months.

Looking ahead, Sheeran’s tour will continue with scheduled performances in other U.S. cities, and his team is already in talks with stadium officials to lock in new dates for the Foxborough shows. Fans can expect an official announcement within the next two weeks, once the weather outlook stabilizes and logistical details are finalized. In the meantime, the artist’s next stop—Chicago’s United Center—remains on track, offering a chance for concertgoers to experience the same high‑energy setlist that was slated for Massachusetts, albeit under clearer skies.
